title: Outlook: custom organisation properties on profile cards
summary: The briefing matches Microsoft's notice and roadmap, including the admin opt-in default and January 2027 rollout targets. Its controls and surrounding people-data guidance are supported, and it distinguishes the existing Entra property API from the new connector-sourced properties without inventing licensing or automation.

claims.claim: Microsoft plans to enrich Outlook profile cards with organisation-specific properties from external systems such as HR platforms.
claims.quote: These properties can be sourced from external systems like HR platforms, enriching user profiles with relevant organizational details.

claims.claim: Learn does not yet describe the specific new connector-sourced custom-property display configuration.

claims.quote: Browse the Connectors gallery in the Microsoft 365 admin center and check the Human resources & recruiting category.

claims.claim: POST https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/external/connections creates an external connection, the operation used for custom people connectors.
claims.quote:
Create a new externalConnection object.
POST https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/external/connections

claims.claim: A people connection uses contentCategory = people as a top-level externalConnection property rather than a property inside configuration.
claims.quote: contentCategory | microsoft.graph.externalConnectors.contentCategory | Specifies the domain category of the content associated with the external connection.

claims.claim: The existing optional-property visibility UI is Settings > Org settings > People settings > Profile card > Contact info.
claims.quote: They're hidden by default, but admins can configure their visibility by navigating to Settings > Org settings > People settings > Profile card > Contact info in the Microsoft 365 admin center.

claims.claim: POST https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/admin/people/profileCardProperties supports directoryPropertyName, annotations and isVisible for existing Entra properties.
claims.quote: Use the annotations and directoryPropertyName properties on profileCardProperty to configure profile card properties. You can also use the isVisible property to indicate whether the given directory property should be shown on a user’s profile card.

claims.claim: The existing profile card API covers Entra properties including CustomAttribute1 through CustomAttribute15.
claims.quote: You can add any of the 15 Microsoft Entra ID custom extension attributes to users' profile cards

claims.claim: Microsoft has not confirmed that the existing Entra profile card property API controls connector-sourced custom properties.
claims.quote: Searched: profile cards connector custom properties visibility display name icon Graph API people custom properties. Opened add-properties-profilecard, Create profileCardProperty and beta profileCardProperty; their documented attributes are Entra properties.

claims.claim: For existing optional properties, hiding a property does not prevent it appearing in other Microsoft 365 experiences.
